label.en: Average monthly salary of the current year

description.en: Represents the national average gross monthly salary (AMS) for the current year in Lithuania, expressed in EUR per month (latest value 2,506.7 EUR). It is also used to cap social-insurance contributions in tpcpi_lt/DefVar.

description.en: The Basic Social Allowance (BSA) — called MSL (minimum standard of living) before August 2008 — is Lithuania's principal reference amount for indexing family and social benefits; its current simulated value is €78 per month. It is used directly as the benefit-formula base for the universal child benefit (bch00_lt/ArithOp) and needs-based child allowances (bchba_lt/BenCalc, bchnm_lt/BenCalc), for the multiple-births benefit (bchmp_lt/BenCalc), and — as a floor expressed in BSA multiples — for the childcare benefit (bmact_lt/ArithOp LowLim, bmact_lt/BenCalc), the maternity benefit (bmaprct_lt/ArithOp lowlim) and the second-parent childcare benefit (bmaed_lt/BenCalc). Per the Country Report, the BSA-based lower limits for maternity/paternity/childcare benefits rose stepwise from 6 BSA (2022) to 7 BSA (2023) to 8 BSA (mid-2023), and BSA itself is uprated annually on the previous year's minimum consumption needs basket (MCNB), moving to a blended MCNB/average-wage-forecast formula from 2026.

description.en: $PensionAgeFemale is Lithuania's official statutory retirement (pension) age for women, used as an age threshold across several spine policies. description.en: $SSI is the monthly State Supported Income (valstybės remiamų pajamų dydis), Lithuania's core reference amount for means-tested minimum-income benefits; per the parameters document it was EUR 221/month in 2025, rising to EUR 233 in 2026 under annual indexation. description.en: This is the per-child coefficient (a multiplier of the Basic Social Allowance, BSA) for the disability-related route of Lithuania's Additional child benefit (bch00_s, 'papildoma išmoka vaikui'), the top-up paid on top of the universal child benefit to families raising a child with a disability. label.en: Birth grant coefficient

description.en: This is the birth-grant coefficient: the number of Base Social Assistance (BSA) units used to calculate Lithuania's one-off birth grant (vienkartinė išmoka gimus vaikui), a non-contributory lump sum paid to one parent, adoptive parent, or guardian per child born. It is used in the bchba_lt policy's BenCalc function as the comp_perElig parameter, which sets the benefit paid per eligible child as this coefficient times the BSA. Per the Country Report the grant equalled 11 BSA per eligible child throughout 2022-2025 (770 EUR in 2025); per the LT benefits description document the coefficient rose to 14 BSA effective 1 June 2026, which matches this constant's current (latest) value of 14. The constant's value has been revised periodically since 2005 (4 recorded values in total), and the benefit itself is not income-tested and not taxable.

label.en: Multiple birth benefit - other

It is consumed in bchmp_lt/BenCalc as the Comp_perTU parameter under the function commented 'eligibility and amount - other cases', so the monthly family benefit equals 12 x BSA. This is consistent with the Country Report and benefits theme description, which state the benefit is 4 BSA for twins and rises by a further 4 BSA per additional child born at the same time (8 BSA for triplets, hence 12 BSA for a fourth child); the benefit is paid to one parent from the birth of the children until they turn 2, is not itself means-tested, but is counted as income in the means tests for social assistance and child benefits.

description.en: This constant is the dimensionless coefficient (multiplier of the Basic Social Assistance amount, BSA) used to compute Lithuania's non-contributory multiple-birth benefit (išmoka gimus vienu metu daugiau kaip vienam vaikui) when triplets are born at the same time. It feeds into bchmp_lt/BenCalc as the Comp_perTU parameter under the function commented 'eligibility and amount - triplets', producing a monthly benefit of 8 x BSA. Per the Country Report and benefits theme description, the benefit starts at 4 BSA for twins and increases by 4 BSA for each additional child born together, so triplets receive 8 BSA; the benefit is paid to one parent from birth until the children reach age 2, is not means-tested itself, but is counted as income when assessing eligibility for the social assistance and child benefits.

label.en: Multiple birth benefit - twins

description.en: This constant is the dimensionless coefficient (multiplier of the Basic Social Assistance amount, BSA) used to compute Lithuania's non-contributory multiple-birth benefit (išmoka gimus vienu metu daugiau kaip vienam vaikui) for the base case of twins. It is consumed in bchmp_lt/BenCalc as the Comp_perTU parameter under the function commented 'eligibility and amount - twins', producing a monthly benefit of 4 x BSA (EUR 280 in 2025 per the Country Report). The benefit, granted for the birth of two or more children at the same time, is paid to one parent from birth until the children turn 2; it is not means-tested itself but counts as income for the social assistance and child benefit means tests, and rises by a further 4 BSA per additional child for triplets and beyond.

label.en: Universal child benefit coefficient

description.en: This is the coefficient (a multiplier of the Basic Social Allowance, BSA) that sets the monthly amount of Lithuania's Universal child benefit (bchnm_s, 'išmoka vaikui'), a non-contributory, non-means-tested cash benefit paid to every family or care institution with one or more dependent children up to age 18 (or up to 23 if in full-time general or vocational education, including while on sick, pregnancy or childbirth-related leave). It is defined in ConstDef_lt and used in the bchnm_lt policy's BenCalc function as the Comp_perElig parameter, i.e. the per-eligible-child compensation multiplied by BSA to produce the benefit amount. Per the Country Report and the LT benefits description, the benefit has been set at 1.75 BSA per child per month since 1 January 2021 (122.5 EUR in 2025), is not subject to an income test, and is not taxable.

description.en: This is the childcare-benefit compensation rate applied during the first 12 months of leave when a parent selects the longer, two-year ('Option I') childcare duration; it is currently 45% and feeds bmact_lt/BenCalc's comp_perElig parameter, commented 'replacement ratio (since 2008)'. According to the Country Report, since 1 January 2023 the two-year childcare-benefit option pays 45% of average monthly insured income (AMII) in the first year and 30% in the second (set by the companion constant $bmact_SecondYear_rate); the 2022 rules (Table 2.6/2.7) used different first/second-year percentages. The resulting amount is additionally bounded by the BSA-based floor ($bmact_LowLim) and AMS-based ceiling ($bmact_MaxLim).

The constant has held its value of 6 (i.e. 6 x BSA, 420 EUR in 2025) since 2005-01-01. In the EUROMOD LT spine it is used in policy bmaed_lt's BenCalc function as the Comp_perElig parameter, i.e. the compensation amount awarded per eligible person, applied to whichever parent is eligible (the mother, or the father if there is no eligible mother).

label.en: maternity leave duration after birth

description.en: This constant fixes the post-delivery portion of the maternity leave period at 56 calendar days. It is used in bmaprct_lt/ArithOp's formula parameter to build the total maternity-benefit entitlement period ('entitlement period (months)'), and separately in bmact_lt/BenCalc's comp_perElig ('benefit duration (days)'), where the childcare benefit's duration is adjusted relative to the end of maternity leave. Per the Country Report, the maternity benefit's applicable period totals 126 calendar days — 70 days before childbirth plus 56 days after delivery (with a further 14 days added for complicated or multiple births, not modelled in EUROMOD) — and childcare-benefit duration is correspondingly reduced by the number of days maternity/paternity benefit was already paid.

description.en: This constant is the statutory number of calendar days of maternity leave granted before childbirth (70 days) under Lithuania's contributory maternity leave benefit (motinystės išmoka), part of the total 126-calendar-day applicable period defined by the Law on Sickness and Maternity Social Insurance (70 days before birth plus 56 days after delivery, with 14 additional days for complicated childbirth or multiple births, though the latter is not simulated in EUROMOD due to data constraints). In the model it is used in the bmaprct_lt policy's ArithOp function as an operand of the 'formula' parameter, whose comment identifies it as computing the benefit's 'entitlement period (months)'. The value has been unchanged at 70 days since 2005-01-01.

label.en: Maternity benefit low lim

description.en: This constant is the statutory minimum (floor) level of the Lithuanian contributory maternity leave benefit, expressed as a multiple of the Base Social Amount (BSA). It is used as the 'lowlim' parameter of the ArithOp function in policy bmaprct_lt that computes the benefit amount (func_comment: 'benefit amount'), i.e. B = daily compensatory salary x 77.58% x number of working days in the applicable period, ensuring the calculated benefit is never paid below this floor. Per the Country Report, the floor was raised from 6 BSA in 2022 to 7 BSA in 2023, and to its current value of 8 BSA since mid-July 2023; the constant has changed 6 times in total since being introduced on 2005-01-01. Although tagged with unit 'currency' in the extracted data, the value itself is a multiplier of BSA rather than an absolute euro amount.

description.en: This constant sets the minimum months of Sickness and Maternity Social Insurance contribution history required for eligibility to the maternity, childcare and pregnancy-grant benefits, currently 12 months. The Country Report states maternity and childcare both require 'no less than 12 months over the last 24 months' of contribution history; paternity's own requirement was also 12 months before 2023 but was reduced to 6 months since 2023, so it is not fully clear from the available sources whether this shared constant still governs paternity's current (lower) threshold or reflects a legacy/common baseline reused across the Elig conditions.

label.en: Maternity, paternity benefit replacement rate

description.en: This constant sets the earnings-replacement rate applied to a recipient's average monthly insured income (AMII) when calculating both the maternity leave benefit (motinystės išmoka) and the paternity leave benefit (tėvystės išmoka), paid under Lithuania's Law on Sickness and Maternity Social Insurance. It is used in bmaprct_lt's ArithOp to compute the maternity benefit amount, and in bplct_lt's ArithOp to compute the benefit amount allocated to fathers, so the same rate underpins both contributory family-leave payments. Per the Country Report (bmaprct.md, bplct.md) and the 2025-2026 benefits description, the rate currently equals 77.58% of the recipient's compensatory income, subject to a floor of 8 BSA (basic social amount) for both benefits and, for paternity benefit, a ceiling of 2 average monthly salaries (AMS); the constant has held one earlier value since records begin in 2005.

label.en: Pregnancy grant coefficient

description.en: This constant is the coefficient (currently 6.43) that is multiplied by the Base Social Amount (BSA) to compute the level of the Lithuanian pregnancy grant (vienkartinė išmoka nėščiai moteriai / bmaprnc_s), a non-contributory lump-sum benefit paid to a pregnant woman at the 28th week of pregnancy when she is not entitled to the social-insurance maternity leave benefit (in EUROMOD, modelled instead as paid to mothers with an own child aged 0). It is consumed in the bmaprnc_lt policy's ArithOp function (formula parameter, commented "benefit amount") to calculate the benefit amount as 6.43 x BSA, equal to 450.1 EUR in 2025; the benefit is not means-tested and not taxable. The coefficient has applied since 2005-01-01 and was unchanged through 2022-2025, though the euro value of the grant still moves each year because the underlying BSA is itself indexed annually (to the minimum consumption needs basket, and from 2026 also to an average-wage growth forecast).

label.en: min no of months in work for paternity benefit since 2023

description.en: This constant holds the minimum number of months of qualifying work/contribution history a father (or adoptive father) must have to be eligible for the paternity leave benefit (tėvystės išmoka), and feeds into bplct_lt's Elig function as part of the elig_cond eligibility test. Per the Country Report, before the first day of paternity leave a father must have no less than 6 months of Sickness and Maternity Social Insurance contribution history over the last 24 months; before 2023 the required period was 12 months, consistent with both the constant's label ('...since 2023') and its two recorded historical values. The Country Report notes that detailed social-insurance contribution records are not available in EUROMOD's underlying data, so this months threshold is applied as a work-history eligibility proxy in the simulation rather than to actual insurance contribution records.

label.en: Paternity benefit duration

description.en: This constant expresses, in months, the period over which the paternity leave benefit entitlement is averaged, and is used in bplct_lt's ArithOp formula to derive the 'benefit amount: average per month' figure. The Country Report and the 2025-2026 benefits description specify that Lithuania's paternity benefit is a lump sum covering 30 calendar days of leave, which can be taken any time between the child's birth and the child turning 1 year old; the constant's current value of 1 (month) reflects this roughly one-month entitlement, used to convert the total lump-sum benefit into EUROMOD's standard monthly income accounting period. The constant has taken two distinct values since records begin in 2005, though current sources consistently describe a stable 30-day duration.

label.en: Normative size of housing: 1st person in hh

description.en: Defines the normative (notional) living-space allowance, in square metres, credited to the first member of a household when the model computes the household's normative dwelling size for the Lithuanian compensation for heating costs (policy xhcht_lt, 'Compensation for heating costs' – a means-tested benefit for excessive heating expenses). It is used in xhcht_lt/BenCalc (parameter Comp_Cond, function comment 'Housing: calculating the normative size (m2) of housing') together with $bsa00_NSSecondPers_sqm and $bsa00_NSSubsPers_sqm to build up a family's total normative floor space. In the current parameterisation the first-person allowance (90 sqm) equals the allowance for a single-occupant household ($bsa00_NS_sqm); the constant has applied since 2005-01-01 and has had 3 recorded values.

label.en: Equivalence scale: first

description.en: $bsa00_scale_coef1 is an equivalence-scale weight of 1 (100%), the share of the first family member's own income counted toward Lithuania's social assistance means test. It is used in bsa00_lt/BenCalc's Comp_perTU parameter, whose internal comment describes this as the 'sum of equivalence scales' methodology in place since 2012, alongside the second-member (90%) and third-and-subsequent-member (70%) weights. Per the Country Report's benefit-amount rules, this full weighting reflects that the first family member's income is counted in full when comparing family income against the 1.1×SSI per-person threshold, unlike the partial disregards applied to additional members.

Per the Country Report's benefit-amount rules, the household benefit for the second family member equals 1.1×SSI (State Supported Income) minus 90% of that person's income — a 10% income disregard that raises the amount payable relative to counting income in full.

label.en: single pensioner benefit

description.en: $bsg_amt is the flat monthly rate of Lithuania's single person benefit (vienišo asmens išmoka, labelled 'single pensioner benefit'; covered in the Country Report as bsg_s), a non-contributory top-up for single adults who either have a working capacity of 55% or less, or have reached statutory pension age, and who do not receive a widow's/orphan's survivor pension (or receive one lower than this amount); before 2022 eligibility instead required receipt of specific pension types or a higher, 60% incapacity threshold. Within the bsg_lt policy it is plugged into BenCalc as the flat-rate amount for single beneficiaries — the sampled usage site is the 'component for single disabled (contributory)' entered via the Comp_Cond parameter — and the same constant is reused a total of 5 times across the policy's parallel components for single beneficiaries (disabled and pensioners, under both the contributory and non-contributory/assistance schemes), always drawn from the base spine, not any add-on. The benefit carries no income test and is not taxable, and is indexed annually to the basic amount of the widow's pension; the LT benefits documentation gives €42.29 per month for 2025 rising to €46.46 per month for 2026, while the model's latest stored value (€50.34) points to a further indexation increase beyond the period covered by that documentation.

label.en: Childcare cost amounts for meals (daily amounts for a five-day week)

description.en: $xcc_amt1 is the gross daily childcare fee (for a five-day week) charged to parents in Lithuania for children younger than 3 (broadly ages 1-2) attending formal, centre-based (municipal) childcare, covering the compulsory meal fee. It feeds the xcc_lt policy's ArithOp function (comment "Childcare cost for children younger than 3"), which computes the gross childcare cost for this younger age band before any discounts are subtracted. Per the Lithuania Net Childcare Costs description, the daily fee for this age group is a fixed amount that is not income-tested and rose from EUR 2.6 in 2025 to EUR 2.9 in 2026 (the current value held by the constant), consistent with municipal fee-setting decisions such as City of Vilnius decision 1-1711/1-305.

label.en: Childcare cost discount rates

description.en: $xcc_ded_rate1 is a discount rate (0.5, i.e. 50%) applied to the gross childcare fee for households qualifying for a partial fee reduction. It is used in the xcc_lt policy's ArithOp function (comment "Calculation of deduction") to derive the deduction subtracted from the gross fee computed via $xcc_amt1/$xcc_amt2. Per the Lithuania childcare cost theme description, a 50% reduction applies to single parents and households with more than two dependent children (2025 rules), with the 2026 rules extending this same 50% discount to families with 3 or more children, children with disability, and households where both parents have a disability (working capacity of no more than 40%); this discount is not itself income-tested.

$xcc_ded_rate2 is a discount rate (1, i.e. 100%) applied to the gross childcare fee for households that qualify for a full fee waiver. It is used, alongside $xcc_ded_rate1, in the xcc_lt policy's ArithOp function (comment "Calculation of deduction") to compute the deduction from the gross childcare fee. Per the Lithuania Net Childcare Costs description, households receiving social assistance benefit from a full (100%) reduction of childcare fees; while the discount is not directly income-tested, eligibility is contingent on receiving the (means-tested) social assistance benefit.
